q: Carbon is found in nature as diamond and _____.
e: Carbon is found in nature as diamond and graphite. Graphite is the idea that completes this fact. Graphene would fill a different blank than graphite.

q: Fullerene and graphene are _____ carbon.
e: Fullerene and graphene are synthetic carbon. Synthetic is the idea that completes this fact. Metallic would fill a different blank than synthetic.

q: If an element can exist in more than one form, in the same physical state, it is said to exhibit _____.
e: If an element can exist in more than one form, in the same physical state, it is said to exhibit allotropy or polymorphism. Allotropy or polymorphism is the idea that completes this fact. Isomerism would fill a different blank than allotropy or polymorphism.

q: The different forms of an element in the same physical state that possess different physical properties are known as _____.
e: The different forms of an element in the same physical state that possess different physical properties are known as allotropes. Allotropes are different forms of the same element, such as oxygen and ozone, or diamond and graphite. Isotopes would fill a different blank than allotropes.

q: Which of the following are allotropes of carbon?
e: Diamond, graphite, fullerene and graphene are allotropes of carbon. Diamond, graphite, fullerene and graphene is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen and ozone are not allotropes of carbon.

q: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by _____ other carbon atoms.
e: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by four other carbon atoms. Four is the idea that completes this fact. Three would fill a different blank than four.

q: Diamond has a giant structure containing millions of carbon atoms in a three dimensional network of strong _____.
e: Diamond has a giant structure containing millions of carbon atoms in a three dimensional network of strong carbon-carbon covalent bonds. A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs. Ionic bonds would fill a different blank than carbon-carbon covalent bonds.

q: The melting point of diamond is _____.
e: The melting point of diamond is 3550 °C. 3550 °C is the idea that completes this fact. 3000 °C would fill a different blank than 3550 °C.

q: Diamond is the _____ among all naturally occurring substances.
e: Diamond is the hardest among all naturally occurring substances. Hardest is the idea that completes this fact. Most conductive would fill a different blank than hardest.

q: In graphite, each carbon atom is surrounded by _____ other carbon atoms in the same plane.
e: In graphite, each carbon atom is surrounded by three other carbon atoms in the same plane. Three is the idea that completes this fact. Four would fill a different blank than three.

q: In graphite, layers of hexagons are weakly bonded to each other through weak forces known as _____.
e: In graphite, layers of hexagons are weakly bonded to each other through weak forces known as van der Waals forces. Van der Waals forces is the idea that completes this fact. Ionic bonds would fill a different blank than van der Waals forces.

q: Due to its layered structure, graphite is soft and has a _____ touch.
e: Due to its layered structure, graphite is soft and has a soapy touch. Soapy is the idea that completes this fact. Metallic would fill a different blank than soapy.

q: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and heat due to the presence of _____.
e: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and heat due to the presence of free electrons. An electron is a tiny negative particle that occupies shells around the nucleus. Protons would fill a different blank than free electrons.

q: The melting point of graphite is _____.
e: The melting point of graphite is 3700 °C. 3700 °C is the idea that completes this fact. 3000 °C would fill a different blank than 3700 °C.

q: Fullerene ($C_{60}$) is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a _____.
a: hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes
e: Fullerene (C60) is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes. Hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes is the idea that completes this fact. Single layer of hexagons would fill a different blank than hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes.

q: Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as _____.
e: Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as Bucky balls. Bucky balls is the idea that completes this fact. Graphene sheets would fill a different blank than Bucky balls.

q: Fullerenes have _____ melting and boiling points than diamond and graphite.
e: Fullerenes have lower melting and boiling points than diamond and graphite. Lower is the idea that completes this fact. Higher would fill a different blank than lower.

q: Graphene is a _____ of graphite.
e: Graphene is a single layer (monolayer) of graphite. Single layer (monolayer) is the idea that completes this fact. Thick block would fill a different blank than single layer (monolayer).

q: Graphene's crystalline structure is _____.
e: Graphene's crystalline structure is two-dimensional. Two-dimensional is the idea that completes this fact. One-dimensional would fill a different blank than two-dimensional.

q: In proportion to its thickness, graphene is about _____ stronger than the strongest steel.
e: In proportion to its thickness, graphene is about 100 times stronger than the strongest steel. 100 times is the idea that completes this fact. 1000 times would fill a different blank than 100 times.

q: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the _____.
e: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the absence of air. Absence of air is the idea that completes this fact. Presence of excess air would fill a different blank than absence of air.

q: Charcoal has a _____ structure and has many small holes.
e: Charcoal has a porous structure and has many small holes. Porous is the idea that completes this fact. Metallic would fill a different blank than porous.

q: Coke is formed by heating coal in the absence of air and is almost _____.
e: Coke is formed by heating coal in the absence of air and is almost pure carbon. Pure carbon is the idea that completes this fact. Pure sulphur would fill a different blank than pure carbon.

q: Carbon black (soot) is left as a residue when kerosene is burnt in a _____ amount of air.
e: Carbon black (soot) is left as a residue when kerosene is burnt in a limited amount of air. Limited is the idea that completes this fact. Sufficient would fill a different blank than limited.

q: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, _____ is formed.
e: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, carbon dioxide is formed. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon monoxide would fill a different blank than carbon dioxide.

q: When carbon burns in a limited amount of air or oxygen, _____ is formed.
e: When carbon burns in a limited amount of air or oxygen, carbon monoxide is formed. Carbon monoxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon dioxide would fill a different blank than carbon monoxide.

q: Carbon can be used as a _____ in the extraction of some metals.
e: Carbon can be used as a reducing agent in the extraction of some metals. Reducing agent is the idea that completes this fact. Oxidising agent would fill a different blank than reducing agent.

q: When strongly heated, carbon can reduce the oxides of zinc to zinc and _____.
e: When strongly heated, carbon can reduce the oxides of zinc to zinc and carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon dioxide would fill a different blank than carbon monoxide.

q: Diamond is used for jewellery because of its _____.
e: Diamond is used for jewellery because of its brilliant shine. Brilliant shine is the idea that completes this fact. Electrical conductivity would fill a different blank than brilliant shine.

q: Powdered graphite is used as a dry lubricant for machine parts which operate at high temperature because graphite is _____.
e: Powdered graphite is used as a dry lubricant for machine parts which operate at high temperature because graphite is non-volatile. Non-volatile is the idea that completes this fact. Soluble in water would fill a different blank than non-volatile.

q: Fullerene is used in artificial photosynthesis, cosmetics, surface coating of medical devices and _____.
e: Fullerene is used in artificial photosynthesis, cosmetics, surface coating of medical devices and drug delivery system. Drug delivery system is the idea that completes this fact. Printing ink would fill a different blank than drug delivery system.

q: Graphene is widely used for solar cells, light-emitting diodes (LED), touch panels and _____.
e: Graphene is widely used for solar cells, light-emitting diodes (LED), touch panels and smart windows or phones. Smart windows or phones is the idea that completes this fact. Printing ink would fill a different blank than smart windows or phones.

q: Activated charcoal is used as an adsorbent in industry for bleaching, deodourization and _____.
e: Activated charcoal is used as an adsorbent in industry for bleaching, deodourization and water purification. Water purification is the idea that completes this fact. Metal extraction would fill a different blank than water purification.

q: Coke is used as a fuel in the metal industry and as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals such as _____.
e: Coke is used as a fuel in the metal industry and as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals such as lead, iron and zinc. Lead, iron and zinc is the idea that completes this fact. Gold, silver and platinum would fill a different blank than lead, iron and zinc.

q: Carbon black is used for making printing ink, black shoes polish and as a filler in _____.
a: vehicle tyres and other rubber products
e: Carbon black is used for making printing ink, black shoes polish and as a filler in vehicle tyres and other rubber products. Vehicle tyres and other rubber products is the idea that completes this fact. Glass manufacture would fill a different blank than vehicle tyres and other rubber products.

q: Carbon is found in nature combined with other elements in petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and _____.
e: Carbon is found in nature combined with other elements in petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and sugar. Sugar is the idea that completes this fact. Salt would fill a different blank than sugar.

q: Carbon is a major component of giant molecules called macromolecules which include proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and _____.
e: Carbon is a major component of giant molecules called macromolecules which include proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and carbohydrates. Carbohydrates is the idea that completes this fact. Minerals would fill a different blank than carbohydrates.

q: Graphite is used in making _____ in the cells.
e: Graphite is used in making electrode in the cells. Electrode is the idea that completes this fact. Separator would fill a different blank than electrode.

q: Graphite crucibles are used as containers for _____ at high temperature.
e: Graphite crucibles are used as containers for melting metals at high temperature. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places. Boiling water would fill a different blank than melting metals.

q: A very small amount of carbon is used to make some types of _____.
e: A very small amount of carbon is used to make some types of steel. Steel is the idea that completes this fact. Cement would fill a different blank than steel.

q: Charcoal is commonly used as a fuel for _____.
e: Charcoal is commonly used as a fuel for cooking. Cooking changes substances in food, so it is everyday chemistry. Driving cars would fill a different blank than cooking.

q: Carbon black is used for making _____ and black shoes polish.
e: Carbon black is used for making printing ink and black shoes polish. Printing ink is the idea that completes this fact. Fertilizer would fill a different blank than printing ink.
